title: Leptospira Isolation from Animal Samples Protocol
author: Gomard Yann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ifccbiw

steps.title: Place kidney in EMJH medium
steps.instruction: After euthanasia, place one kidney into a sterile microtube containing 1.0 mL EMJH + AFAS + 5‑FU; store the tube at room temperature until dissection is completed.

steps.title: Ethanol surface sterilization
steps.instruction: Transfer the freshly dissected kidney into a 1.5 mL tube containing 1.0 mL 70 % ethanol and soak for 30 seconds to remove surface contaminants.

steps.title: Rinse kidney in sterile water
steps.instruction: Move the kidney to a microtube with 1.0 mL sterile water and rinse for 30–60 seconds to eliminate ethanol.

steps.title: Slice kidney on sterile dish
steps.instruction: Place the kidney on a sterile petri dish; using a sterile scalpel (and optionally a sterile tip to hold the organ), cut a transverse slice approximately 1 mm thick.

steps.title: Excise cortex‑medulla‑pelvis piece
steps.instruction: Within the 1 mm slice, cut a small piece that includes cortex, medulla, and renal pelvis.

steps.title: Crush tissue with scalpel
steps.instruction: Using a disposable scalpel, crush the piece for 1–5 minutes (longer is better); add 100–200 µL EMJH + AFAS + 5‑FU to aid slicing, aiming for the finest possible fragments.

steps.title: Transfer suspension to EMJH tube
steps.instruction: With a sterile 1000 µL filtered tip, aspirate the tissue‑fluid mixture and dispense it into a microtube already containing 1.0 mL EMJH + AFAS + 5‑FU (final volume 1–1.2 mL). Preserve any remaining kidney tissue in a sterile tube at –20 °C/–80 °C or in 70 % ethanol at room temperature for later DNA extraction.

steps.title: Room‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: Keep the microtube at room temperature for 45–60 minutes, avoiding direct sunlight; invert the tube gently every 15 minutes to mix.

steps.title: Aliquot into three culture tubes
steps.instruction: After the 45–60 minute incubation, invert the tube to mix and pipet 250 µL of the suspension into each of three Falcon® culture tubes, each pre‑filled with 2.5 mL of one of the three media (i, ii, iii) described in the reagents section. Optionally dilute each inoculated tube ten‑fold (e.g., 250 µL into 2.5 mL of the same medium) to reduce contamination risk. For urine‑based isolation, inoculate 2–4 urine droplets into each of the three tubes.

steps.title: Incubate inoculated tubes
steps.instruction: Store the three inoculated tubes in an incubator set to 28 °C. For field work without power, keep the tubes in a polystyrene box to minimise temperature fluctuations until laboratory facilities are available.

steps.title: Microscopic examination week 1
steps.instruction: After one week of incubation, place a drop of each inoculated medium on a clean microscope slide and examine under a dark‑field microscope for the presence of Leptospira.

steps.title: Weekly monitoring for four months
steps.instruction: Repeat the dark‑field microscopic examination weekly for up to four months, recording any positive observations.

steps.title: Sub‑culture positive isolates
steps.instruction: For tubes that test positive, transfer 1.0 mL of the culture into 3.0–5.0 mL of fresh medium (i, ii, or iii) that does not contain 5‑FU.

steps.title: Handle contaminated positives
steps.instruction: If a positive culture shows contamination by other microorganisms, either sub‑culture into fresh liquid medium containing 5‑FU or filter the culture through a sterile syringe equipped with a 0.22 µm filter.

steps.title: Long‑term storage of isolates
steps.instruction: Store isolates by (a) freezing 1.0 mL of the Leptospira culture at –80 °C or in liquid nitrogen, or (b) inoculating 5.0 mL Fletcher medium + RS 8 % (medium iii, without 5‑FU) with 100–500 µL of the culture; the latter can be kept at room temperature for up to six months.

steps.title: Dispose of consumables
steps.instruction: Discard used pipette tips, disposable scalpel, and petri dish in an appropriate laboratory waste container.
